hexdump

Hexadecimal file dump (back in DataReel 7.4, from 6.x): show a binary file, rebuild it from the dump, checksums and number conversions.

Contents

Usage
Examples

Usage

hexdump [switches] infile [outfile]
  -a     a C array          -d   decimal (8 bytes a line)    -s   no comments (the ; text column)
  -c     CRC-32             -C   CRC-16 (ARC/XMODEM) and CCITT CRC-16
  -p#    pause every # lines on the console
  -r     rebuild a binary file from a hex dump: hexdump -r dump.txt out.bin (checked with a CRC-32)
  -xHEX  -XHEX (signed)  -BHEX (binary)  -DDEC: number conversions

The dump: 16 bytes a line as two hex digits each, then a tab, "; " and the printable bytes ("." for the others). The formats and the switches are the 6.x ones, so a dump made by the 6.x hexdump rebuilds with this one and the reverse; the checksums are the 6.x values.

Examples

A small text file, notes.txt, holding two lines: "DataReel 7.4" and "hexdump test".

$ hexdump notes.txt
44 61 74 61 52 65 65 6C 20 37 2E 34 0A 68 65 78 	; DataReel.7.4.hex
64 75 6D 70 20 74 65 73 74 0A                   	; dump.test.

$ hexdump -c notes.txt
notes.txt
CRC-32 = 0xE92728C4

$ hexdump -C notes.txt
notes.txt
CRC-16 = 0xDEA1
CCITT CRC-16 = 0x3332

$ hexdump -a notes.txt
unsigned char CArray[26] = {
  0x44,0x61,0x74,0x61,0x52,0x65,0x65,0x6C,0x20,0x37,0x2E,0x34,0x0A,0x68,0x65,0x78,
  0x64,0x75,0x6D,0x70,0x20,0x74,0x65,0x73,0x74,0x0A
};

Save the dump in a file, then rebuild the binary file from it (the rebuilt file is the same, byte for byte):

$ hexdump notes.txt notes.hex
$ hexdump -r notes.hex notes.bin
Building new binary file from hex dump text file...
Finished.
26 bytes written to notes.bin
$ cmp notes.txt notes.bin && echo same
same

Number conversions:

$ hexdump -xFF
0xFF = 255
$ hexdump -D255
255 = 0xFF
$ hexdump -B1010
0x1010 = 0000 0000 0000 0000 0001 0000 0001 0000
